# A global and integrated analysis of CINSARC-associated genetic defects

## Description

The CINSARC signature is a transcriptomic marker that identifies high-risk soft-tissue sarcomas, associated with high metastatic potential. During the last decade, CINSARC has been successfully developed and validated and is currently being assessed in two prospective phase 3 clinical trials for stratification of therapy. Though the link between CINSARC expression and tumour aggressiveness is well established, questions remain about how CINSARC genes are regulated. In this study, we leveraged TCGA multi-omics study on sarcomas with complex genetics to appraise the association between CINSARC profile, genomic features and two potential regulation mechanisms: DNA methylation and miRNA expression. We demonstrate that CINSARC expression is associated with an increase of ploidy, intra-tumour heterogeneity, copy-number alteration and expression of 37 miRNAs, and a decrease of DNA methylation. These genetic changes are not independent, but act together to promote or repress CINSARC expression. These findings depict new insights into CINSARC regulation.

### Note 1:
Please use the most recent version of this repository.

### Note 2:
Because *TCGAbiolinks* needs to download thousands of files, we provide scripts we used to do so and output data already agregated into Rdata files (*Processed_Rdata* folder).

### Note 3:
Here is the list of packages required to plot information from Rdatas: *survival*, *scales*, *limma*, *FactoMineR*, *factoextra*, *fmsb*, *plotrix*, *vioplot*, *grid* and *psych*.

Here is the additional list of packages to rerun all analyses from scratch: *parallel*, *doParallel*, *foreach*, *TCGAbiolinks*, *dplyr*, *topGO*, *ChAMP*, *cluster*, *Biobase*, *SummarizedExperiment*, *DT*, *data.table*, *IlluminaHumanMethylation450kanno.ilmn12.hg19* and *org.Hs.eg.db*.[exit code: 0]

Figure_1=function(OUTFILE,C1COL,C2COL) {
  ####################################################################
  # Function to plot a KM estimate with statistical metrics - Fig 1A #
  ####################################################################
  myKM=function(a,col_Event,col_Time,col_Pred,MAIN,C1COL,C2COL,
                modifiedYlab="Metastasis-free survival",modifiedC1lab="low-risk profile",
                modifiedC2lab="high-risk profile",
                xlab="Time (years)",lwd=2) {
    stopifnot(col_Event %in% colnames(a))
    stopifnot(col_Time%in% colnames(a))
    stopifnot(col_Pred %in% colnames(a))
    stopifnot(identical(c("C1","C2"),sort(unique(as.character(a[,col_Pred])))))
    if (is.character(a[,col_Pred])) a[,col_Pred]=factor(a[,col_Pred],levels=c("C1","C2"))
    index=which(apply(a[,c(col_Event,col_Time,col_Pred)],1,function(x) length(which(is.na(x) | x=="")))>0)
    if (length(index)>0) a=a[-index,]
    rm(index)
    C1=length(which(a[,col_Pred]=="C1"))
    C2=length(which(a[,col_Pred]=="C2"))
    eC1=length(which(a[,col_Pred]=="C1" & a[,col_Event]==1))
    eC2=length(which(a[,col_Pred]=="C2" & a[,col_Event]==1))
    SD=survdiff(Surv(a[,col_Time], a[,col_Event])~a[,col_Pred]) # p log-rank
    stopifnot(length(SD$n)-1==1) # 1 degree of freedom
    Pval=pchisq(SD$chisq,1,lower.tail=F)
    COXPH=summary(coxph(Surv(a[,col_Time], a[,col_Event])~a[,col_Pred])) # Cox PH
    HR=round(COXPH$conf.int[1],2)
    HR_CI_DN=round(COXPH$conf.int[3],2)
    HR_CI_UP=round(COXPH$conf.int[4],2)
    rm(COXPH)
    sur.all=survfit(Surv(a[,col_Time],a[,col_Event])~strata(a[,col_Pred]),data=a) # Kaplan-Meier
    plot(sur.all,col=c(C1COL,C2COL),ylab=modifiedYlab,xlab=xlab,las=0,xaxs='i',xlim=c(-0.05,10.05),
         main=MAIN,lwd=lwd,cex.main=2,mark.time=T,cex.lab=1.25)
    text(x=max(a[,col_Time])/2,y=1,labels=paste0("HR = ",HR," [",HR_CI_DN,"-",HR_CI_UP,"]"),cex=1.125)
    text(x=max(a[,col_Time])/2,y=0.94, labels=bquote(italic(P)['log-rank'] ~ "=" ~ .(scientific_format(3)(Pval))), cex=1.125)
    legend('bottomleft',legend=c(as.expression(bquote(.(modifiedC1lab)~"("*italic(n)*.("=")*.(C1)*"):"~.(eC1)~events)),
                              as.expression(bquote(.(modifiedC2lab)~"("*italic(n)*.("=")*.(C2)*"):"~.(eC2)~events))),
           lwd=lwd,pch="-",bg="white",cex=1.125,border=NA,col=c(C1COL,C2COL),bty='n')
  }
  
  #####################################
  # Function to vioplot CNAs - Fig 1B #
  #####################################
  myBoxPlot=function(VEC1,VEC2,MAIN,C1COL,C2COL) {
    par(cex.lab=1.25)
    vioplot(VEC1,VEC2,col=c(C1COL,C2COL),names=c("C1","C2"),ylim=c(0,1600),plotCentre="line",
            ylab="Segments with |mean|>0.2",main=MAIN,cex.main=2,xlab='CINSARC',las=0)
    text(1.5,1600,bquote(italic(P)["Welch's t-test"] == .(scientific_format(3)(t.test(VEC1,VEC2)$p.value))),
         cex=1.125)
  }
  
  ############################################################
  # Function to display the penetrance plot of CNAs - Fig 1C #
  ############################################################
  myPP=function(SNP6,CHRsize,cytoband,MAIN,C1COL,C2COL) {
    par(mar=c(0,4.2,3.15,2.1))
    plot(NULL,xlab="",ylab="",xlim=c(0,CHRsize$cumul[22]),ylim=c(-1,1),yaxt="n",xaxt="n",xaxs="i",yaxs="i",
         main=MAIN,axes=F,cex.main=2)
    rect(cytoband$Start_ADJ,0.8,cytoband$End_ADJ,-1,border=NA,col=cytoband$color)
    abline(v=CHRsize$cumul[1:21])
    par(mar=c(2.1,4.2,0,2.1))
    plot(NULL,xlab="",ylab="",xlim=c(0,CHRsize$cumul[22]),ylim=c(-100,100),yaxt="n",xaxt="n",xaxs="i",yaxs="i")
    points(SNP6$pos_adjusted,SNP6$GAIN_C1*100,pch=16,cex=0.25,col=C1COL)
    points(SNP6$pos_adjusted,SNP6$GAIN_C2*100,pch=16,cex=0.25,col=C2COL)
    points(SNP6$pos_adjusted,-SNP6$LOSS_C1*100,pch=16,cex=0.25,col=C1COL)
    points(SNP6$pos_adjusted,-SNP6$LOSS_C2*100,pch=16,cex=0.25,col=C2COL)
    axis(2,at=seq(-100,100,50),labels=round(abs(seq(-100,100,50))),cex.axis=1,las=0)
    mtext(c("Gains (%)","Losses (%)"),side=2,line=3,at=c(50,-50),cex=0.825)
    abline(h=0)
    abline(v=CHRsize$cumul[1:21])
    axis(1,at=CHRsize$middle[1:22],1:22,las=1,cex.axis=0.75,las=2)
    par(mar=c(2.1,4.2,0,2.1))
    plot(NULL,xlab="",ylab="",xlim=c(0,CHRsize$cumul[22]),ylim=c(0,3),yaxt="n",xaxt="n",xaxs="i",yaxs="i")
    points(SNP6$pos_adjusted,-log10(SNP6$P),type="l",lwd=0.75,col="grey50")
    mtext(bquote("FET (adjusted "*italic(P)*")"),side=2,line=2.75,at=1.5,cex=0.825)
    axis(2,at=c(0,-log10(0.05),3),labels=c(1,0.05,'1e-3'),cex.axis=1,las=0)
    abline(h=-log10(0.05),lty=3,col="red",lwd=1.5)
    abline(v=CHRsize$cumul[1:21])
    axis(1,at=CHRsize$middle[1:22],1:22,las=1,cex.axis=0.75,las=2)
    box()
  }
  
  ####################
  # Code starts here #
  ####################
  print('Plotting figure 1')
  load('../data/Misc/CHRsize_hg38.Rdata')
  load('../data/Misc/cytoband_hg38.Rdata')
  load('../data/Processed_Rdata/clinical.Rdata')
  load('../data/Processed_Rdata/SNP6.Rdata')

  png(OUTFILE,width=17.5,height=17.5,units='cm',res=300,pointsize=12)
  layout(matrix(c(1,2,3,3,4,4,5,5),ncol=2,byrow=T),widths=c(0.5,0.5),heights=c(0.5,0.08,0.25,0.17))
  par(mar=c(4.2,4.2,3.15,2.1))
  myKM(clinical,"META","META_DATE","CINSARC",'A',C1COL,C2COL,
       modifiedC1lab="CINSARC C1",modifiedC2lab="CINSARC C2") # Here is Fig 1A
  myBoxPlot(clinical$CNA[which(clinical$CINSARC=='C1')],
            clinical$CNA[which(clinical$CINSARC=='C2')],
            'B',C1COL,C2COL) # Here is Fig 1B
  myPP(SNP6,CHRsize,cytoband,'C',C1COL,C2COL) # Here is Fig 1C
  dev.off()
}[exit code: 0]

Figure_2=function(OUTFILE,C1COL,C2COL) {
  #########################################
  # Function to barplot vectors - Fig 2A #
  #########################################
  myBarP1=function(vec1,vec2,ylim,MAIN,C1COL,C2COL) {
    vec1[which(vec1>=1)]='At least 1 WGD'
    vec1[which(vec1=='0')]='No WGD'
    TAB=table(vec2,vec1)[c('C1','C2'),c('No WGD','At least 1 WGD')]
    a=barplot(TAB,col=c(C1COL,C2COL),ylab='Number of samples',ylim=ylim,cex.lab=1.25,main=MAIN,cex.main=2)
    legend("topright",legend=c("C1","C2"),title="CINSARC",fill=c(C1COL,C2COL),bty="n",border=NA,cex=0.9)
    legend("top",legend=bquote(italic(P)["Fisher's"]==.(scientific_format(3)(fisher.test(TAB)$p.value))),
           cex=0.9,x.intersp=0)
  }
  
  #########################################
  # Function to barplot vectors - Fig 2B #
  #########################################
  myBarP2=function(vec1,vec2,THRESH,ylab,ylim,MAIN,C1COL,C2COL) {
    ORDER=order(vec1,vec2)
    vec1=vec1[ORDER]
    vec2=vec2[ORDER]
    rm(ORDER)
    a=barplot(vec1,col=ifelse(vec2=="C1",C1COL,C2COL),ylim=ylim,ylab=ylab,cex.lab=1.25,main=MAIN,cex.main=2)
    legend("topleft",legend=c("C1","C2"),title="CINSARC",fill=c(C1COL,C2COL),bty="n",border=NA,cex=0.9)
    abline(v=mean(a[THRESH:(THRESH+1)]))
    legend("top",legend=bquote(italic(P)["Fisher's"]==.(scientific_format(3)(fisher.test(table(replace(rep(0,length(vec1)),1:THRESH,1),vec2))$p.value))),
           cex=0.9,x.intersp=0)
  }
  
  ###############################################
  # Function to vioplot vectors - Fig 2C and 2D #
  ###############################################
  myBoxP=function(vec1,vec2,ylab,ylim,MAIN,C1COL,C2COL) {
    par(cex.lab=1.25)
    vioplot(vec1~vec2,col=c(C1COL,C2COL),xlab="CINSARC",plotCentre="line",
            ylab=ylab,ylim=ylim,main=MAIN,cex.main=2)
    legend("top",legend=bquote(italic(P)["Welch's t-test"]==.(scientific_format(3)(t.test(vec1~vec2)$p.value))),
           bty="n",x.intersp=0,cex=0.9)
  }
  
  ####################
  # Code starts here #
  ####################
  print('Plotting figure 2')
  load('../data/Processed_Rdata/clinical.Rdata')
  clinical=clinical[which(!is.na(clinical$Ploidy)),]
  
  png(OUTFILE,width=17.5,height=17.5,units="cm",res=300,pointsize=12)
  layout(matrix(c(1,2,3,4),nrow=2,byrow=T))
  par(mar=c(2.1,4.2,3.15,1.05))
  myBarP1(clinical$WGD,clinical$CINSARC,c(0,49),"A",C1COL,C2COL) # Here is Fig 2A
  myBarP2(clinical$Ploidy,clinical$CINSARC,44,"Ploidy",c(0,5),"B",C1COL,C2COL) # Here is Fig 2B
  par(mar=c(4.2,4.2,3.15,1.05))
  myBoxP(clinical$Mut,clinical$CINSARC,"Mutation load",c(0,225),"C",C1COL,C2COL) # Here is Fig 2C
  myBoxP(clinical$ITH,clinical$CINSARC,"Intra-tumour heterogeneity",c(0,0.85),"D",C1COL,C2COL) # Here is Fig 2D
  dev.off()
}[exit code: 0]
